schema.description: One period's heart rate metrics from healthdata.db, as the health ETL summarised them: every heart-group metric it holds for one day, week, month or year. Written by the health-db worker; values are the ETL's numbers as stored, never recomputed by Anam. Version 4 requires source_time, every other rule unchanged. No writer sends this type any more: the health-db worker and its ETL retired, and its facets are tombstoned.

group.description: The source's metric group id (metrics.group_id). Always "heart" for this type.

metrics.description: The period's heart metrics, keyed by the ETL's metric id (summaries.metric_id): hr, rhr, inactive_hr and the separate hr_min, hr_max, rhr_min and rhr_max. The source's bp_systolic and bp_diastolic are left out by the worker, because health.blood-pressure carries the readings. Garmin and Withings both write hr into the same source row, so it holds whichever ran last.

additionalProperties.description: One metric's row in the source's summaries table for this period.

avg.description: summaries.avg_value. For a Garmin metric, GarminDB's own figure for the period; for a Withings metric, the mean of the period's measurements, computed by the ETL.

max.description: summaries.max_value. Null when the source has no range for the metric. Garmin ranges are GarminDB's own columns; Withings ranges are the ETL's maximum over the period.

min.description: summaries.min_value. Null when the source has no range for the metric. Garmin ranges are GarminDB's own columns; Withings ranges are the ETL's minimum over the period.

samples.description: summaries.sample_count: how many Withings measurements the ETL aggregated, or 1 for every Garmin row.

unit.description: metrics.unit for this metric id, as the ETL's metric table defines it.

period_start.description: summaries.period_start as the source's own text: local midnight on the period's first day, no zone. Weeks start on Monday. This is the fact time.

period_type.description: summaries.period_type: the length of the period summarised.

source_time.description: How the health ETL's clock was read: value is summaries.period_start, local midnight on the period's first day as the ETL wrote it with no zone, read in Australia/Sydney, the Definition's zone. The ETL never said which zone it meant, so a facet says basis assumption. No writer sends this type any more (the health-db worker retired); a facet written again must say how its clock was read.

value.description: The fact time as the source supplied it, as text and never rewritten: a date, a wall clock, an RFC 3339 string, or an epoch as its digits.

zone.description: The zone value is read in, and nothing else: an IANA name when one is known, UTC for a value that is UTC, else a fixed offset +HH:MM or -HH:MM. The gate refuses a name that is no zone.

basis.description: Who decided the zone. source: the source supplied it with the value, or the value is UTC by the source's own definition. configuration: a setting a person made for this source names it. assumption: the importer or writer chose it, with nothing behind it but its own default or the Definition's zone, and logged that it did.
